chapter_theme: The first quarter of Agappei Siddhar's songs, each stanza a four-line address to the inner demon (அகப்பேய்), the ego-mind that must be told to keep quiet. After a frame (take in no poison, fear not, say nothing) the poet runs through the Saiva map of manifestation, the Supreme becoming the worlds, nada and bindu, the five elements with their colours, the organs, the ten nadis, the letters அ உ ம, the adhvas and the fifty-one letters, and after each item says that it is not the Lord: all of it is a built thing (சகலம்), the four paths and the thirty-six tattvas included, and only knowing oneself, with the sadguru's feet, is the way.
structure_note: 1642 is the frame; 1643 to 1659 is the catalogue of manifestation (Supreme and worlds 1643, nada and bindu 1644 to 1645, the four paths 1646, the three groups of five 1647 to 1649, the six and the three 1651, the elements and their colours 1652 to 1654, the letters 1655 to 1656, the adhvas and fifty-one letters 1657 to 1658, the tattvas 1659); 1660 to 1666 turn the list into a negation: none of this is the Lord, the religions and the thirty-six do not avail, and the way is to know oneself, not sariyai or kiriyai.

1642.reading: Do not swallow poison, demon within; to gain the Lord's feet, do not let the heart waver, and say nothing at all.
1642.nuance: அகப்பேய் (the demon within) is the addressee of every stanza, traditionally the ego or restless mind; the feminine -அடி endings treat it as a girl spoken to. நஞ்சு may be plain poison, or the poison of the senses and the world as tradition takes it; the stanza also sets the rule the whole work repeats, that the demon is to be silent.

1643.reading: It is the Supreme beyond the supreme, demon; it came as the wide sea, and it alone created the netherworld and the seven worlds.
1643.nuance: பராபரம் is the Siddhars' usual name for the Supreme beyond gods; பரவை (the sea, per the gloss) may be the ocean of manifestation or the formless expanse, and the stanza makes creation its unaided act.

1644.reading: Nada is the Veda, demon; have you seen the good dance? The foot is Shakti, and the para-bindu is nada.
1644.nuance: The stanza stacks equations from the Saiva cosmogony: nada as the first scripture, the dancing foot as Shakti, bindu as the source of nada. The order (பரவிந்து நாதமடி) could also mean that bindu and nada are both named; tradition has nada rise from bindu.

1645.reading: Bindu and nada, demon, came as the real (or as body); the five great elements became their seat.
1645.nuance: மெய் is both 'truth' and 'body'; the elements as the seat (இடம்) of bindu and nada fits the body reading, in which the subtle pair takes gross form in the five elements. The gloss printed under this stanza (நாலுபதம்) belongs to 1646.

1646.reading: You have seen that the four paths are the good way, demon; but unless it is the root, it is not release.
1646.nuance: நாலு பாதம் is glossed as sariyai, kiriyai, yoga and jnana. The stanza grants them as a good way and denies them as release unless they reach the மூலம் (root), which 1656 names as the letter சி and 1706 denies altogether; the poet's view of the paths unfolds in 1666, 1667 and 1676.

1647.reading: The five that begin with speech, demon: hear how they came; they are an aggregate, and they are not the truth.
1647.nuance: வாக்காதி ஐந்து are the five organs of action (speech, hands, feet, excretion, generation), as the gloss says. ஒக்கம் (a gathering, an aggregate) is the stanza's reason for denying them truth: they are a compound, not the one.

1648.reading: The five that begin with sound, demon, became the sastras; they are also falsehood, and I have told you the truth.
1648.nuance: சத்தாதி ஐந்து are the five subtle elements (sound, touch, form, taste, smell). Saying they 'became the sastras' puts learning on the side of the senses, and மித்தை (false) condemns both together.

1649.reading: The five that begin with vasana came in strength, demon; the ten nadis are ten, and see that this is firm.
1649.nuance: வசனாதி ஐந்து is unclear: it may be the five organs of knowledge (completing the groups of five in 1647 and 1648), or a corruption of a word for the five vital airs. தெசநாடி, the ten nadis, is a standard count in the yogic body.

1650.reading: All that is cause, demon, I have told as I saw it; you have seen the destruction too, and all the ways in which they came.
1650.nuance: காரணம் gathers the causes listed so far. மாரணம் is killing or destruction (in tantric lists one of the six rites); here it most likely means that everything that came also perishes.

1651.reading: The Agamas told of the six tattvas, demon; and the unchanging mandalas came as three.
1651.nuance: ஆறு தத்துவம் may be the six adhvas (paths) of the Agamas, the thirty-six tattvas counted as six sixes (as ஆறாறு in 1664), or the six adharas. The three unchanging mandalas are traditionally sun, moon and fire, placed in the body as well as the cosmos.

1652.reading: Earth is golden in colour, demon, and this is no ignorance; water's form, what is within it, is white.
1652.nuance: The colour scheme for the five elements, begun here and finished in 1654, follows the tantric table also found in the Tirumanthiram: earth gold, water white, fire red, air dark, sky smoke. பேதமை அல்ல insists this is knowledge, not fancy.

1653.reading: Fire is red, demon, see that this is firm; air is blue, and I will tell you the matter of the sky.
1653.nuance: நீலம் (blue, or dark) for air matches the 'black' of the Tirumanthiram's table; the colours are the meditator's signs for the elements in the body, as tradition takes them, rather than observations.

1654.reading: The sky is cloud-coloured, demon; hear how it came, let there be no defect, and I have told you what is.
1654.nuance: வான மஞ்சு could be 'the sky is yellow' or 'the sky is cloud (smoke-coloured)'; the Tirumanthiram's table gives the sky தூமம், smoke, so the second reading is likelier. ஊனம் ஆகாதே warns against error in the sequence.

1655.reading: All this arose as the letter அ standing there, demon; the letter உ joined it and it came to have form.
1655.nuance: அகாரம் and உகாரம் are the first two letters of Om; the stanza makes them the stages of manifestation, அ as the first arising and உ as form. அங்கென்று (as 'there') is obscure; it may mean that with அ a 'there', a place, first appeared.

1656.reading: The letter ம is maya, demon, and I have told you it is impurity; the letter சி is the root, so reflect on it.
1656.nuance: The third letter of Om is read as maya and malam, matching the Saiva key in which the ம of நமசிவாய stands for impurity, while சி (of சிவ) is the root. 1684 revisits the letters with அ as anava.

1657.reading: Letters and worlds, demon, mantras and tantras: I will tell you more, and you will listen with a murmur of assent.
1657.nuance: வன்னம் (varna), புவனம் (bhuvana) and மந்திரம் are three of the six adhvas of Saiva Siddhanta; தந்திரம் stands for the Agamic rites. இம்மென்று கேட்பாயே asks the demon to hear without talking back, in keeping with 1642.

1658.reading: From the elephant to the line, demon, and the fifty-one letters: you have seen that they are falsehood, so do not believe them true.
1658.nuance: அத்தி வரை is obscure; the gloss offers elephant or nadi for அத்தி, and the phrase may mean 'up to the elephant' (the whole range of created things) or a drawn line. The fifty-one letters of the Sanskrit alphabet, which the Tirumanthiram treats as the stuff of the mantra-path, are here called மித்தை.

1659.reading: The tattvas, demon, came as the whole of things; I have told you the intellect too: are they not the form of the elements?
1659.nuance: சகலம் is 'everything' and also the Siddhanta name for the soul's state when joined to all the tattvas. Even buddhi, the intellect, is brought under the elements, so that no inner faculty escapes the catalogue.

1660.reading: All these kinds, demon, are not our Lord; that kind is another, so inquire and see.
1660.nuance: The pivot of the chapter: everything listed since 1643 is set aside as not the Lord. அந்த விதம் வேறே leaves what the Lord is unsaid, and ஆராய்ந்து makes inquiry, not instruction, the way to it.

1661.reading: If sin is to end, demon, you must not keep imagining; there is no dying either: it is the sadguru's feet.
1661.nuance: பாவிக்க means to imagine or to meditate on a form; the stanza forbids it, as 1731 does. சாவதும் இல்லை may promise freedom from death through the guru, or state that there is no death to fear; the two clauses are joined only by the refrain.

1662.reading: However much is said, demon, my mind is not consoled; leave both the conscious and the unconscious, and bring them together and see.
1662.nuance: சித்து and அசித்து are spirit and matter; the stanza asks to leave both and then சேர்த்து (join, or gather) and see, perhaps to see them as one from beyond them. The confession that no telling consoles the mind is unusual in the poet's voice.

1663.reading: The six religions, demon, came of their own making; inquire and tell me the place where you stand settled.
1663.nuance: சமய மாறு is the six Saiva or six orthodox religions; தம்மாலே வந்தவை says they are human constructions. The demon is asked where it rests, not which sect it holds.

1664.reading: The thirty-six exist, demon, but I have told you they do not avail; if there is something else, tell it truly.
1664.nuance: ஆறாறு, six sixes, is the thirty-six tattvas. The poet grants that they are (ஆகும்) and denies that they help (ஆகாது), the same move as with the four paths in 1646.

1665.reading: When you know yourself, demon, you will join with nothing; I will tell you what is, the way to know yourself.
1665.nuance: Self-knowledge is offered as the one thing the catalogue did not contain, and its mark is non-attachment (ஒன்றையும் சேராயே). The promise of a method is kept in 1666 to 1668 as a series of denials.

1666.reading: Sariyai will not do, demon: you have seen that it gives salokam; even if you do kiriyai, nothing is gained.
1666.nuance: The stanza accepts the Siddhanta mapping of sariyai to salokam (dwelling in the Lord's world) and values it at nothing: a graded release short of union counts as no gain. 1667 and 1676 do the same for yoga.

links.note: The Tirumanthiram gives earth gold, water white, fire red, air black and the sky smoke-coloured; Agappei's 1652 to 1654 give the same table with air as நீலம் and the sky as மஞ்சு (cloud). The Siddhar takes the Tirumanthiram's meditative table as settled doctrine and then, in 1660, says none of it is the Lord.

Tirumular says that by three letters the light springs up and by the great letter (ம) delusion came; Agappei says ம is maya and impurity while சி is the root. Both read the letters of the mantra as a key to bondage and release, and both assign delusion to ம.

Tirumular counts fifty-one letters, eighty-one words and the rest as the way the adhvas, the paths the soul traverses, came to be; Agappei says the fifty-one letters are falsehood and are not to be believed. The conflict holds if Tirumular's verse treats the letter-path as real; it dissolves if his count is only descriptive of what the knower must pass beyond.

Tirumular says salokam comes with sariyai and sarupam by the further paths; Agappei accepts that sariyai yields salokam and adds that this is nothing gained. He keeps the Siddhanta mapping and strips it of worth.

Sivavakkiyar gives the full ladder, sariyai to salokam, kiriyai to samipam, yoga to sarupam and jnana to sayujyam; Agappei names the first rung and says kiriyai gains nothing, and in 1676 denies yoga too. Where Sivavakkiyar grades the paths, Agappei discards all but knowing oneself.

Tirumular says Saivam is knowing oneself and reaching Siva, and leaving what does not reach him; Agappei says that when you know yourself you join with nothing. Both make self-knowledge the heart of Saivam and detachment its sign; 1696 makes the identification explicit.

source_issues: 1645: the GLOSSES entry (நாலுபதம் - சரியை, கிரியை, யோகம், ஞானம்) belongs to 1646, which has the phrase நாலு பாதம்.
1649 line 1 வசனாதி ஐந்து does not match any standard group of five and may be corrupt.
1658 line 1 அத்தி வரைவாடி is hard to construe; the gloss itself offers two unrelated senses for அத்தி.
